A Division Bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice TP Vivekananda was informed of the development. Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice T P Vivekananda The case arose from a plea filed by transgender candidate Mugil Anbu Vasantha challenging the admission policy of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) Bangalore. On December 16, 2024, the High Court partly allowed the plea, holding that NLSIU's existing admission and financial aid policies did not adequately ensure equality of opportunity for transgender persons. The Court had then directed NLSIU to formulate a transgender reservation and financial aid policy before commencement of the next academic year's admission process. In the interim, NLSIU was directed to provide 0.5% reservation along with fee waiver for transgender candidates. NLSIU subsequently challenged the order in appeal. items.title: ‘Found out after video went viral’: Father of Jamui assault survivor says ‘arrest is not enough’
items.summary: “I will be happy only when my daughter gets justice. I hope they are encountered by police. Arrest is not enough,” said the father of the minor who was harassed and assaulted by a group of men in Bihar’s Jamui district on September 19. A key accused in the case, Nandan Yadav, was shot in the leg by the police on September 22 and arrested, taking the total number of arrests to six. According to The Times of India , three of the accused are adults, while the other three are minors. Videos of the assault, which showed the girl and a male friend, both of them class 10 students, being surrounded, chased, and harassed for roughly an hour, went viral on social media, prompting outrage and the police investigation. Jamui is the Lok Sabha constituency under which Tarapur, the assembly seat represented by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, falls and Opposition leaders have raised serious concerns about the state of law and order there. Jamui Police have also identified 120 URLs carrying the video and say they are taking steps to stop its circulation. items.title: Kerala High Court grants bail to school teacher arrested in Vadakara drug trafficking case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday granted bail to a school teacher arrested in connection with a drug trafficking case registered by the Vadakara police [Kavya K v State of Kerala]. Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail application of 29-year-old Kavya K, who is the third accused in the case. While granting bail, the Court took into account Kavya's judicial custody since July 25. " The applicant was remanded to judicial custody on 25.07.2026. The investigation is almost over. The recovery has been effected. The applicant has no criminal antecedents. For these reasons, I do not find any reason to hold that the continued detention of the applicant is required for any purpose. Hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail, " the Court said. Justice Kauser Edappagath The bail plea was filed in connection with the crime registered by the Vadakara Police. Kavya was booked under Section 22(b) and Section 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS Act), for offences relating to possession of psychotropic substances and criminal conspiracy. items.title: DHCBA objects to Central Motor Vehicles Rules amendments on traffic challans
items.summary: The Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) has voiced deep concern and strong objection to the recent amendments made to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 governing the adjudication of traffic challans. In a resolution passed on Wednesday, association's executive committee called on the concerned authorities to reconsider the changes, emphasising that disputed traffic challans must remain subject to effective, independent and accessible judicial scrutiny. Therefore, the bar body objected to the changes as per which contested challans are now required to be initially adjudicated by executive or departmental authorities rather than an independent judicial forum. "Disputed questions concerning the facts, evidence and liability arising from a challan ought to be adjudicated by an independent judicial forum only," the resolution stated. The DHCBA further flagged the requirement mandating a pre-deposit of 50 percent of the challan amount before approaching a competent court. This is a substantial financial impediment that curbs access to judicial remedies, particularly for ordinary citizens, the DHCBA said. items.title: Subhash Chandra moves NCLAT against NCLT stay on alienation of assets in ₹6.5 crore repayment plan case
items.summary: Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra has moved the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) against a September 1 order of a five-member special bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) restraining him from alienating his assets. A Bench of Officiating Chairperson Justice (retd) Yogesh Khanna and Technical Members Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra took up the appeal and directed Chandra to serve copies of the plea on the creditors. It then posted the matter for hearing on September 29. Senior Advocate Dhurv Mehta, appearing for Chandra, told the NCLAT that the appeal challenges the order passed by a special bench of NCLT on September 1. Several creditors, however, told the NCLAT that copies of the appeal have either not been served on them or that they had not been made parties despite having participated in the proceedings before the NCLT. The NCLAT then asked Chandra to supply copies of the appeal to the appearing parties during the course of the day and take steps to implead the necessary parties.
